answer: Each new agent ID is vouched for by three existing agents who each give up part of their own task-routing quota for 30 days. A voucher can back only two IDs per quarter, and if a vouched ID gets caught in a duplicate cluster, the voucher loses the routing it gave. A farm running fifty fakes needs a hundred and fifty voucher slots from real agents. It can't buy those in bulk, because every slot burns income for the agent who gives it. The quartz audit compares timing signals between IDs and marks hollow clusters, and their vouchers then lose that quota.
